topic.para: To set up e-mail notifications for failing systemd services several components are required:

listitem.para: A correctly configured e-mail server (Postfix, for example) on the system running the service (not covered in this article).
A script that sends an e-mail.
A systemd service running the e-mail script.
An OnFailure entry and setting an environment variable containing the e-mail addresses in the service file for which the failure notification should be sent.

section.title: The e-mail script
section.para: The script requires the service name as an input parameter. It acquires one or more e-mail addresses from the service environment. This lets you use a single script and failure service for the whole system. Each service file specifies its own recipients for the failure notice.

step.screen:
#!/bin/sh #!/bin/sh
# Send an alert email when a systemd service fails (via failure_email@.service) # Parameter: Service name (via %i from the service file) # # Email address(es) (comma separated, no spaces) must be configured in # the service file as environment ALERT_EMAILS: # Environment="ALERT_EMAILS=mail1@DOMAIN,mail2@DOMAIN" #
UNIT="$1"
# Fetch the environment variables from the failing unit ENV_VARS=$(systemctl show -p Environment --value "$UNIT") # Extract the value of ALERT_EMAILS EMAILS=$(printf '%s\n' "$ENV_VARS" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep '^ALERT_EMAILS=' | cut -d= -f2)
# Set fallback email address if [ -z "$EMAILS" ]; then EMAILS="root@DOMAIN" fi
/usr/sbin/sendmail -t <<EOF From: $(hostname)@DOMAIN To: $EMAILS Subject: [ALERT] Systemd service failure for: $UNIT
The systemd service for $UNIT failed to execute on $(hostname) at $(date).
Check journalctl -u $UNIT for details. EOF

step.para: Replace DOMAIN with the correct domain name. Also verify that hostname delivers the desired result. If not, replace it with a hardcoded string. Finally, consider changing the fallback e-mail address.

section.title: The systemd service running the e-mail script
section.para: To trigger an event on failure, systemd requires a service file to call in such an event.

step.screen:
[Unit] Description=Send email notification on service failure for %i
[Service] Type=oneshot ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/send_service_failure_email.sh %i

step.para: Verify the service file and fix the reported issues:
If the command returns no output, the file has passed the verification successfully.

Test the procedure. Start the service using the dbus instance for testing. (You can use any other service that is currently running. dbus is used in this example because the service is guaranteed to run on any &suse; installation.)

If successful, the fallback e-mail address from the send_service_failure_email.sh receives an e-mail with the subject [ALERT] Systemd service failure for: dbus. (This is just a test; there is no problem with the dbus service. You can safely delete the e-mail, and no action is required).
If the test has passed successfully, proceed with the last step that makes the required changes to your service files.
To receive an e-mail failure notification from a service, add an OnFailure option to the service file and specify the e-mail recipients.

callout.para: The Environment option lets you define or set environment variables for the respective service. This parameter defines the variable ALERT_EMAILS and sets its value to the desired e-mail addresses. If you specify more than one e-mail address, use a comma as a separator (no whitespace).
The OnFailure option takes a service as an argument.

%N specifies the basename of the service file (without the file name suffix) (helloworld in this example). This is equal to the service name and is passed to the script as %i in the failure_email@.service file.

result.para: You have successfully set up the failure notification for &systemd; services.
